meeting_header:
Date: 2026-07-10 | Time: 16:00 - 16:58 (PDT) | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Jordan Ma (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Dylan Reyes (VP Eng, Falken), Marta Liu (Head of Legal), Omar Patel (SRE), Leah Chen (Procurement)
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Ma: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time today... [intro]
00:12 Dylan Reyes: Thanks, Jordan. Quick note, Marta is here for legal signoff, Leah from procurement, Omar for infra. Our timeline is end of July for go/no-go.
00:27 Jordan Ma: Great, today we'll run through MSA/DPA questions, SLAs, pricing and next steps; Priya will cover the infra bits.
01:03 Priya Kapoor: Hi all. On the dedicated side we can offer reserved GPU pools, and for private deployment there's V P C options — sorry VPC, hmm transcript glitch — with customer-managed KMS integration.
01:35 Marta Liu: On the DPA, our main asks: data residency in EU, sub-processor list, deletion SLA for logs, and auditing access. Is Redwood willing to commit to 30 day deletion for logs?
02:12 Jordan Ma: We can do configurable retention. For hosted we have default 90 days, dedicated/private customers can contract shorter retention — 30 days should be possible as an addendum.
02:48 Leah Chen: On pricing, our finance team needs committed monthly capacity pricing and overage rates. We also need to know if there's a one-time onboarding fee.
03:25 Jordan Ma: Typical structure is monthly commit for Dedicated with a small onboarding professional services fee. I'll include a line-itemized quote — Priya, can you call out typical numbers?
03:40 Priya Kapoor: For a mid-size workload like yours, rough ballpark is 4-8 dedicated GPUs for steady traffic, with burst to shared pools. Pricing varies by region; I'll email the spreadsheet.
04:10 Marta Liu: Liability cap is important. We usually push for three months of fees cap, but we'd want to see indemnity carve-outs for third party data breaches.
04:45 Jordan Ma: Redwood's standard is 12 months of fees as liability cap; enterprise can negotiate. We are open to specific carve-outs; we'll mark that as redline item.
05:20 Omar Patel: From infra perspective latency SLOs are critical. We saw you mention P95 200ms — is that across hosted or dedicated?
05:42 Priya Kapoor: P95 figures depend on model and seq length; for dedicated with our optimized runtime we've hit P95 sub-200ms for common LLMs under test. We'll share benchmark CSVs. Note that KV cache warm vs cold affects tail latency.
06:15 Dylan Reyes: Also need to confirm SOC 2 Type II report and pen-testing cadence. We do vendor security reviews.
06:36 Jordan Ma: Yep we'll share SOC2 and penetration test summary; we can include details about audit logs and traceability. Some transcript artifacts: 'KV cash' in auto notes.
07:05 Marta Liu: About sub-processors: need complete list and 30 days notice before adding any new ones.
07:30 Jordan Ma: We have a public sub-processor list and we can agree to 30 day notice in the DPA addendum for enterprise customers.
08:00 Leah Chen: Procurement process: we'll need MSA, DPA, pricing worksheet, and PO process. Our legal will redline MSA and expects to return within 5 business days.
08:25 Jordan Ma: Great — action: we'll send consolidated package, include a clean and redline MSA for ease. Also I can include a sample SLA addendum showing uptime, remedies, and credits.
09:05 Priya Kapoor: On private deployments, network egress and data flow diagrams will be required for our networking team to review. Omar can you share your network diagram?
09:40 Omar Patel: I'll prepare a network diagram and current infra inventory and share with Priya.
10:05 Dylan Reyes: Any competitors or alternatives being considered? We ran a pilot with OpenAI and looked at Bedrock for multi-cloud support.
10:25 Jordan Ma: Understood. Our differentiator is predictable economics and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private.
11:00 Marta Liu: Regarding deletion and logging, does Redwood provide a mechanism for certifying deletion on request?
11:18 Jordan Ma: Yes, we provide deletion APIs and can issue an attestation for deletion events as part of the DPA addendum for dedicated/private installs.
12:00 Leah Chen: For SLAs, what uptime guarantee and credits are typical?
12:20 Jordan Ma: Standard enterprise SLA is 99.9% with credits defined per incident; for higher tiers we can go to 99.95 with a higher commitment. We'll share exact SLA table.
13:10 Priya Kapoor: Also flag: model version pinning and rollback policies are available; we can route requests to cheaper model variants as fallback to maintain uptime.
13:55 Dylan Reyes: Latency regressions are a big risk — would like automatic rollback thresholds tied to canary metrics.
14:18 Priya Kapoor: We support canary rollouts with automatic rollback if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds; we'll document what metrics trigger rollback.
15:00 Marta Liu: For DPA, please include encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS and key revocation processes.
15:30 Jordan Ma: Noted, we'll include KMS integration details and key rotation options.
16:05 Omar Patel: Any SLA for data egress times? We need guarantees for bulk export/restore windows.
16:30 Priya Kapoor: We can commit to export window SLAs in the addendum depending on dataset size; standard is 48-72 hours for multi-GB exports; can be negotiated.
17:05 Leah Chen: On pricing approvals: our finance needs a final quote by 2026-07-15 to secure budget for July billing cycle.
17:28 Jordan Ma: We'll aim to deliver final pricing and addenda by 2026-07-15; if not, we'll request an interim approval.
18:10 Dylan Reyes: Any blockers on security posture? Also will you allow an external penetration test against a dedicated staging environment?
18:35 Priya Kapoor: We support customer-led pen tests under NDA and with agreed scope; coordination with our infra team is required.
19:00 Marta Liu: We'll review redlines and escalate any critical legal points; thanks everyone.
19:20 Jordan Ma: Recap: Redwood to send MSA/DPA + SOC2 + pricing + SLA addendum; customer to provide network diagram, traffic profile, procurement timeline. Next meeting tentatively week of 2026-07-20 for technical deep dive and final legal check.
19:50 Meeting end.
notes: Meeting recorded via Fireflies.ai; automated transcript has occasional transcription artifacts (V P C/VPC, KV cash). References to shared artifacts: link: /redwood/docs/security/SOC2.pdf (placeholder), /redwood/benchmarks/dedicated-pricing.xlsx (placeholder).
